entries.core_move: Formulate the continuous-time convolution integral $y(t)=(x*h)(t)=int_{-infty}^{infty} x(\tau)h(t-\tau) d \tau as the LTI system output obtained by integrating weighted$, shifted impulse responses.
Distinguish $\tau$ as the integration variable that scans input and impulse-response overlap from t as the output time in the continuous-time convolution integral.
Treat t as a fixed output-time parameter while letting $\tau$ vary to set up the convolution integrand $x(\tau)$$h(t-\tau)$ for a continuous-time LTI system.
Rewrite each signal's formula and active time interval using $\tau$ as the integration variable so it can be placed correctly in the continuous-time convolution integral.

Trace how an input contribution $x(\tau)$d $\tau$ at time $\tau$ produces the time-invariant system response $x(\tau)$$h(t-\tau)$d $\tau$, justifying $h(t-\tau)$ as the impulse response shifted to each impulse location in the convolution integral.

Execute the flip-shift-multiply-integrate procedure by holding t fixed, forming $h(t-\tau)$, multiplying it by $x(\tau)$, and integrating over $\tau$ to set up a continuous-time LTI convolution output.
Interpret each convolution output value as the signed area of the product over the $\tau$-interval where $x(\tau)$ overlaps the flipped-shifted impulse response $h(t-\tau)$.
